detailed_description: The JavaScript Beautifier is a syntactic parser that transforms raw JavaScript code into human-readable or optimized machine-readable formats. Using Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analysis, it tokenizes input code to reconstruct structured indentation, reinsert optional semicolons, and normalize spacing around operators. Users can toggle between beautification (expanding one-liners into multi-line statements with configurable indentation levels) or minification (removing whitespace and comments while preserving functionality). This tool uniquely supports modern ES6+ syntax including arrow functions, template literals, and JSX expressions, while offering granular controls for comment preservation and variable name obfuscation during minification. Developers require this tool to reverse-engineer compressed production code for debugging, standardize team codebases, reduce file sizes for browser delivery, or analyze legacy scripts with inconsistent formatting.
usage_steps: Open the editor and paste your JavaScript code into the left-hand input panel
Select 'Beautify' or 'Minify' mode using the toggle switch above the editor
Adjust indentation settings (2/4 spaces, tabs) via the dropdown menu
Enable 'Preserve Line Breaks' checkbox to maintain original paragraph spacing
Click the 'Process Code' button to apply transformations in real-time
Copy the output from the right-hand results panel or download as .js file
usage_examples: Debugging a production error by expanding minified code to locate syntax issues
Standardizing code formatting across a team's GitHub pull requests
Reducing JavaScript payload size for mobile app assets
Converting legacy jQuery scripts to modern ES6 module syntax visually
